components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true

      properties:

          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:

          type: string

      required:
        - id

      properties:

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin

          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepted with spaces, dashes
            and brackets and an optional leading '+' country code; stored and returned in
            E.164 form (a leading '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits). When no country code is
            given, '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` behavior for `POST /api/owners` following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**Behavior**: When a create request sets `sharesHousehold: true` and an existing owner already shares its household (same last name + address, compared case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed), the request is allowed and both the new owner and the existing member(s) are assigned the same stable `householdId`, which is returned on the owner. Without the flag, a household duplicate is still rejected with 409 (unchanged).

**Changes**:
- **`OwnerHouseholds.java`** (new package-private helper) — the single definition of household membership (`members(...)`) and the stable id derivation (`householdId(...)`, a 12-char hex prefix of SHA-256 over the canonical last name + address, so every member computes the same value regardless of creation order). This removes the `canonical`/matching logic that was duplicated in the reject step.
- **`RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold.java`** — refactored to delegate membership detection to `OwnerHouseholds`.
- **`AssignOwnerHousehold.java`** (new function) — when opted in and a household exists, assigns the shared id to the built owner and persists it onto existing members lacking it. Wired into `owners.POST.yml` as a new `assignHousehold` step after `assignCustomerCode`, under the same transaction.
- **`Owner.java`** — added the `household_id` persisted field with accessors.
- **`openapi.yml`** — added `householdId` as a read-only field on the `Owner` schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps it on the response).
- **`OwnerMapper.java`** — ignore `householdId` when mapping the request DTO to an entity (consistent with `customerCode`).
- **schema.sql** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the `household_id` column.

I also fixed a latent bug in the id derivation: `String.format("%02X", digest[i])` sign-extends negative bytes, so I masked with `& 0xFF`.

The dedicated acceptance test (`coreJoinersShareHouseholdId`) and the full `./mvnw test` suite pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
